title: G-Class W463
verdict: Twenty-eight years and engines from four to twelve cylinders, all on the same ladder frame and two solid axles. It became a rapper's accessory and stayed a real off-roader the whole time. Buy one for the three lockers and keep a budget for the vacuum lines.

paragraphs: The W463 is the G-Class most people picture: square, upright, faintly absurd, and still built on a ladder frame with a solid axle at each end. Between 1990 and 2018 it went from a farmer's tool with a wood dash to a twin-turbo V12 AMG with more than 600 PS, a 6×6 cousin and a Maybach landaulet. Mercedes fitted it with more engine types than any other model it has built, and it never lost the three locking differentials that make it so good off-road.

story.heading: FRANKFURT, 1989: THE G GETS A LIVING ROOM
paragraphs: For the G's tenth birthday, Mercedes showed a new version at the 1989 Frankfurt show, and production started the following April. It had a new chassis number, W463, and a new mission. Permanent four-wheel drive replaced the [[g-class/w460|W460]]'s part-time system, the diff locks became electrically switched from the middle of the dash, ABS was available, and for the first time the cabin got wood and leather. Autocar's 1991 test said permanent 4WD and ABS made it 'a much more convincing tool on the road.'

The working trucks went elsewhere. The W463 dropped the panel vans and barn doors, and they carried on in the utilitarian [[g-class/w461|W461]] for armies and agencies. Early W463s used carryover engines, with petrol 230 GEs and 300 GEs and diesel 250 GDs and 300 GDs. In 1994 the line was renamed the G-Class, the manual gearbox disappeared, and ventilated front discs and a driver's airbag became standard.

story.heading: V8s, AMERICANS AND AMG
paragraphs: Mercedes started testing what the G could carry. The 1993 [[g-class/500ge|500 GE]] squeezed in a V8 for a run of 446 trucks. In 1996 an electronically controlled five-speed automatic arrived, and the 1997 update brought V6 engines and dual airbags. The [[g-class/g500|G 500]] made the V8 a regular-production option in 1998, and in 1999 the [[g-class/g55-amg|G 55 AMG]] became the most powerful G yet.

America came next, by a back door. Mercedes didn't sell the G in the US, so Europa International of New Mexico started certifying and selling them in 1993. Those [[g-class/europa|Europa trucks]] proved the demand, Mercedes bought the distribution rights, and the G launched officially in the US with the 2002 model year. That facelift brought ESP, Brake Assist and the four-wheel electronic traction system, 4ETS.

story.heading: LUXURY, LOCKERS AND A LOT OF CYLINDERS
paragraphs: From there the W463 kept adding power. The G 55 AMG got a supercharger in 2004, the 5.5-litre M273 V8 created the US [[g-class/g550|G 550]] for 2009, and in 2012 came the twin-turbo G 63 and the V12 G 65. Mercedes sold just over 100 G 63 6×6s, and the portal-axled [[g-class/4x4-squared|G 500 4×4²]] followed in 2015. Ninety-nine Maybach G 650 Landaulets closed out the run. By the end there were 22 paint colours and engines from four to twelve cylinders, naturally aspirated, supercharged, turbo and twin-turbo.

Underneath, almost nothing changed. The frame, the solid axles and the three lockers were the same on a 2018 G 550 as on a 1990 230 GE. Hagerty quotes 36°/31° approach and departure angles, 80% grades and 30° side slopes for the G. Handsome Motors, a dealer who has owned more than 200 Gs, estimates that each truck still took roughly 100 hours of hand labour in Graz.

story.heading: HOW IT ENDED
paragraphs: In late 2017 Mercedes announced the end of the first-generation W463. Its replacement, revealed at Detroit in January 2018, kept the shape, the ladder frame and three lockers. It also brought independent front suspension, rack-and-pinion steering and the first formal crash test of any G. The [[g-class/second-gen|second generation]] is the better road car by a wide margin.

For the trail crowd, though, 2018 marks the last year a new G came with a solid front axle. That's why clean W463s, from the 1990s diesels to the last [[g-class/g550|G 550s]], are now bought as off-roaders as much as status symbols.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE G THAT WOULDN'T DIE
callout.title: How the US Marine Corps saved the W463
paragraphs: Mercedes announced that 2005 would be the G-Class's last year in America, naming the new GL-Class as its successor. It shipped 500 farewell Grand Edition G 500s and G 55 AMGs, and rumours spread that W463 production would end entirely: emissions and pedestrian-safety rules were tightening, and the military contracts were complete.

Then the US Marine Corps ordered 157 G-based Interim Fast Attack Vehicles, and enthusiasts protested loudly. On 11 November 2005 Dieter Zetsche announced the G would continue. At the 2006 Paris show Mercedes promised production through 2015, then extended Magna Steyr's contract to 2017. The 'replacement' GL is long gone, and the G is still in production.

engineering_intro: Mercedes never changed the W463's hard parts. A separate ladder frame carries the body, coil springs suspend a rigid axle at each end, and the recirculating-ball steering box comes from the same family as the W460's. Drive goes to all four wheels all the time through a two-speed transfer case. The three locks are where the complexity lives: an electronic controller enforces the order (centre, then rear, then front), vacuum engages the centre lock and switches the valves, and hydraulic slave cylinders on the axles slide dog sleeves into the front and rear diffs. An auxiliary vacuum pump backs up the engine's own vacuum.

buying_checks.head: Rust, rust, rust
buying_checks.body: Handsome Motors lists the places to check: the roof around the sunroof, the metal under the tail-lights and rear door, every door hinge, the rear spring perches, the windscreen gasket, the mirror bases, the 'dog-leg' cavities inside the doors and every body seam. Autocar adds the inner wheel arches and the area around the rear bumper.

buying_checks.head: Test all three lockers
buying_checks.body: Engage centre, rear and front in order on loose ground and watch the indicators. Lockers that 'were never used' often don't work. Handsome Motors says to have the hydraulics flushed before chasing parts; vacuum leaks are the next suspect.

buying_checks.head: Drive it at 55–70 mph
buying_checks.body: Judder or shaking can mean a failing propshaft (Autocar budgets £1,500 or more). Harsh 2–3 shifts, flares or speed-sensor codes on the five-speed 722.6 point to old fluid or a failing conductor plate.

buying_checks.head: Early-2000s electrics
buying_checks.body: Handsome Motors says 2002–04 trucks suffer seat-motor, window-regulator and door-lock-actuator gremlins, along with transfer case motor and actuator faults, and that these improved each year until 2005–06. Test every switch.

buying_checks.head: A sagging headliner means water
buying_checks.body: Handsome Motors notes that 2002 US trucks have a hard fibreboard headliner while 2003-on trucks got a fabric one that is probably sagging by now. Autocar warns a sagging headliner can also mean water is getting in, so check the sunroof drains, the rear-door hinge seals and the fuse box area for damp.

buying_checks.head: Listen for a thump
buying_checks.body: Coil springs crack, especially in cold weather, and a loud thump over bumps is the sign. Autocar puts the fix at about £120 per corner.

buying_checks.head: Engine-specific weak spots
buying_checks.body: M113 (G 500, early G 55): harmonic balancer and viscous fan. M273 (G 550, 2009–15): starters every 50–60k miles, cam magnets and intake swirl flaps. M176 (2016–18): a failed crankcase-vent oil separator can cause rear-main and valve-cover leaks, with $3–5k in labour for the rear main seal (Handsome Motors). M157 G 63: inspect the cooling system and water pump.

buying_checks.head: Is it really an AMG?
buying_checks.body: Autocar warns about standard Gs converted to look like AMGs. Check the VIN and the factory data card, not the badges.

repairs.title: Lockers won't engage: find the vacuum leak
repairs.cost: Often a few dollars in fittings; vacuum reservoir ≈$74 (Expedition Imports)
repairs.symptoms: One or more lock lights never come on, the centre lock drops out (and takes the rear with it), or locks release when engine revs fall.
repairs.fix: Follow the MBWorld owner who fixed his 2005 G 500. Pull the vacuum hose at the transfer case and test for vacuum there. Then work back toward the source: intake manifold, the vacuum reservoir in the front-left wheel well, then the switchover valve block on the firewall, teeing a gauge into each segment. His leak was a split plastic connector inside a rubber Y-piece under the brake booster. Replace brittle hoses and weak check valves as you go, then flush and bleed the hydraulic side.
repairs.tools: Hand vacuum pump with gauge · tee fittings · vacuum line and connectors · diff-lock vacuum reservoir 102 070 00 68 if cracked · brake bleeder for the hydraulic slaves

repairs.title: Centre diff lock vacuum diaphragm
repairs.symptoms: Vacuum reaches the transfer case but the centre lock still won't engage, or a hand pump on the actuator won't hold vacuum.
repairs.fix: With the truck safely supported, test the centre-lock actuator on the transfer case with a hand vacuum pump. If it leaks down, replace the diaphragm unit, reconnect the lines and confirm the centre lock engages and the light comes on before testing rear and front. G-luxe Travel films the job on a W463 G 500.
repairs.tools: Hand vacuum pump · replacement centre-lock vacuum diaphragm for your transfer case · basic metric sockets · video: G-luxe Travel

repairs.title: Transfer case actuator motor
repairs.symptoms: Low range won't select or deselect, a warning on the dash, or the shift sits half-done. Handsome Motors flags transfer case motors and actuators as a weak spot on 2002–04 trucks.
repairs.fix: Confirm the fault with a diagnostic scan, then unbolt the actuator motor from the transfer case, fit the new unit, then clear the codes and test the range shift with a scan tool. Service the transfer case fluid at the same time, because specialists note owners tend to put it off.
repairs.tools: Mercedes-capable scan tool · replacement actuator motor · transfer case fluid to spec · video: G-luxe Travel 'W463 Transfer Case Fix'

repairs.title: Propshafts: grease, flex discs, judder
repairs.cost: Grease is cheap; Autocar budgets £1,500+ for a replacement shaft
repairs.symptoms: Vibration or judder at speed, clunks on take-up, cracked rubber flex discs, notchy U-joints.
repairs.fix: Grease the propshaft joints and slip yokes at every service; G-luxe Travel has a quick W463 guide. Inspect the flex discs (guibos) and the centre support bearing. Replace flex discs in pairs if either looks marginal, and recheck the bolt torque after a few hundred miles. A shaft that still judders after that needs rebuilding or replacing.
repairs.tools: Grease gun with needle adapter · new flex discs and bolts · torque wrench · centre-drive-shaft bolt N000000006359 / nut N910113010003 as needed

repairs.title: Cracked coil springs (front and rear)
repairs.symptoms: A loud thump over bumps, a corner sitting low, a visibly broken coil, often after a cold snap.
repairs.fix: Support the chassis on stands and take the axle on a jack. Disconnect the shock and sway-bar link on that side, then lower the axle slowly until the spring comes free, watching the brake hoses, ABS wires and locker lines. Fit the new spring with its isolator, raise the axle, and refit the shock and link. Replace springs in axle pairs. G-luxe Travel has front and rear DIY videos on a G 500.
repairs.tools: Floor jack and stands · spring compressor if needed · matched springs · new shocks if tired · videos: G-luxe Travel

repairs.title: 722.6 transmission service and conductor plate
repairs.symptoms: Harsh 2–3 shifts, flares, limp mode, speed-sensor codes such as P0715, ATF wicking up the harness.
repairs.fix: If the service history is unknown, service it now: drop the pan, replace the filter and pan gasket, replace the electrical connector sleeve (the usual oil-wicking point), refill with MB 236.14 ATF and set the level hot. If speed-sensor codes persist, a failing conductor plate is a common cause. For the later seven-speed (2007-on), Handsome Motors advises fluid changes every 40–50k miles.
repairs.tools: ATF to MB 236.14 · filter and pan gasket · connector sleeve · dipstick tool and thermometer or scan tool for level setting

repairs.title: Viscous fan clutch (M113 G 500)
repairs.symptoms: Temperature climbs in traffic or on slow trails, or the fan freewheels easily with a hot engine (or roars all the time).
repairs.fix: With the engine cold, check the fan for wobble and how it resists turning. Hold the pulley and undo the fan clutch from its hub, fit the new clutch and refit the shroud. G-luxe Travel's 'How I won the battle with my viscous fan' covers the G 500 job.
repairs.tools: Fan-clutch holding tool and wrench · replacement viscous coupling · video: G-luxe Travel

repairs.title: Front axle service (bearings, kingpins, swivel seals)
repairs.symptoms: Grease or oil weeping from the steering-ball swivels, torn CV boots, wheel-bearing play.
repairs.fix: Strip each front corner: hub, wheel bearings, kingpin bearings, steering-ball gasket and wipe seals, inner axle seal and bushing, CV and boot. Expedition Imports sells separate kits for 2001-and-older and 2002-and-newer W463s, and 2002-on trucks use a different lower kingpin bearing.
repairs.tools: W463 front axle service kit for your year · kingpin bearing kit (to 2001) or the 2002-on kit · steering-ball wipe seal 460 331 01 80 · axle shaft bushing 463 337 00 49 · W463 hub-nut socket

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: About 33 inches. Expedition Portal owners report a 275/70R18 on an unlifted G 500 and a 285/65R18 with only a slight rub at full left lock. One owner says he has run 315/75R16s on his G 500 for nearly a decade with no lift and no rubbing, but that's an outlier. Wheel offset matters: one owner's rubbing went away when he swapped ET63 wheels for ET43 G 550 wheels, while another says ET63 wheels tuck the rear tires better on 35s. JWO designed its 4-inch springs specifically to clear tires bigger than 33 inches.

faq.q: Which W463 engine is the most reliable?
faq.a: Handsome Motors ranks it G 500 → G 55 → G 550 → G 63 for mechanical reliability, and calls the 2002–2015 V8s the safest bets. In Europe, Autocar names the G 320 CDI diesel V6 the best all-rounder. Avoid neglected G 63s unless you've budgeted for big brakes and cooling-system work.

faq.q: Which years are the best to buy?
faq.a: In the US, a 2005–08 G 500. Handsome Motors says the 2002–04 trucks suffer electrical gremlins (seat motors, window regulators, door-lock actuators, transfer-case actuators) that were mostly gone by 2005–06, and Expedition Portal owners tell the same story about 2002–03. CarGurus adds that the very last 1999–2000 Europa G 500s are considered very reliable, and that 2009-on trucks have fewer problems than the early US ones. The 2016–18 twin-turbo trucks are a reliable option, Handsome Motors says, but not the most reliable. In Europe, Autocar's pick is the G 320 CDI.
faq.src: HANDSOME MOTORS · CARGURUS · EXPEDITION PORTAL · AUTOCAR

faq.q: How do the three lockers work, and in what order?
faq.a: You press the dash buttons and a controller engages them in sequence: centre first, then rear, then front. Each one locks after the truck has rolled a short distance. Vacuum operates the centre lock and the valves; hydraulics move the front and rear locks. Unlock everything before you're back on pavement.

faq.q: Was the W463 sold in the US before 2002?
faq.a: Yes, but not by Mercedes. Europa International of New Mexico federalised and sold them from 1993, and became the exclusive US importer of the G 500 with small-volume-manufacturer status. Those trucks have US VINs. Mercedes took over with the 2002 model year.

faq.q: When did the manual gearbox disappear?
faq.a: In 1994, when the 200, 230 and 300 GE were dropped. From 1996 the automatic was an electronically controlled five-speed. The seven-speed came in for 2007 on the US G 500.

faq.q: Which years have ESP and traction control?
faq.a: ESP, Brake Assist and the four-wheel electronic traction system (4ETS) arrived with the 2001–02 update that coincided with the official US launch. Earlier W463s have ABS but rely on the lockers alone for traction.

faq.q: How often should I service the automatic?
faq.a: Toolsource cites a 40–60k-mile interval for the five-speed 722.6, using MB 236.14 ATF. Handsome Motors suggests every 40–50k miles for the seven-speed. If the history is unknown, do it now.

faq.q: Are the 2016–2018 G 550s with the twin-turbo V8 a good buy?
faq.a: Handsome Motors says yes. The M176 is a lower-stressed relative of AMG's M177, and by those years the early electrical gremlins were gone. Watch for a failed crankcase-vent oil separator causing rear-main-seal and valve-cover leaks. The same dealer personally recommends 3–5k-mile oil changes. For outright reliability, though, he still rates the 2002–2015 trucks higher.
It's an enthusiast label for the 2018-on [[g-class/second-gen|second-generation]] G, which kept the W463 chassis code. Mercedes doesn't use the term itself.

faq.q: How do I spot a fake AMG?
faq.a: Check the VIN and the factory data card. Bumpers, flares, wheels and badges are easy to bolt on, and Autocar specifically warns about Gs converted to look like AMGs.

faq.q: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
faq.a: No. Locked diffs stop the wheels turning at different speeds, so on grippy surfaces the driveline binds and the tires scrub. Use them on dirt, sand, snow or rock at low speed.

mods.why: Two inches levels and firms up a loaded truck. JWO designed its four-inch springs to clear tires bigger than 33 inches.
Once lifted, adjustable Panhard bars re-centre the axles and fresh radius-arm bushings remove wander.
A bolt-on, 4×4²-style conversion: 6 inches of lift and 40 mm more wheel offset.

Diesels, AMGs and 2007-on seven-speed trucks differ, so confirm capacities and approvals in WIS or the owner's manual for your VIN.
